paras.en: Here is how a worm cyberattack works. A malware worm squirms through the internet, copying itself onto whatever systems it can hijack. Hackers can then mine hijacked systems directly for their data or link them together into a botnet and use its computing power, often to send spam email or overwhelm websites with traffic, knocking them offline.
paras.zh: 以下是蠕虫网络攻击的工作原理。恶意软件蠕虫在互联网中蠕动，将自身复制到它可以劫持的任何系统上。然后，黑客可以直接挖掘被劫持的系统以获取数据，或将它们链接到僵尸网络中并利用其计算能力，通常会发送垃圾邮件或淹没网站，导致其离线。

paras.en: Historically, computer worms have been small, simple programs preprogrammed to take advantage of specific security weaknesses. So they could only get into devices that had that weakness. When defenders patched a worm’s target, it could no longer spread. With an AI model directing its actions, however, a worm can adapt and learn on the fly, choosing its line of attack depending on the device, says Guan, of the University of Toronto.
paras.zh: 从历史上看，计算机蠕虫都是经过预先编程的小而简单的程序，以利用特定的安全弱点。所以他们只能进入有这个弱点的设备。当防御者修补了蠕虫的目标后，它就无法再传播。然而，多伦多大学的关说，有了人工智能模型指导其行动，蠕虫就可以动态适应和学习，根据设备选择攻击路线。

paras.en: That adaptability enables the worm to burrow into many different types of devices, both experiments showed. When hackers unleash AI from afar, they orchestrate what the model does. An AI worm that copies itself widely could hypothetically escape anyone’s control.
paras.zh: 两项实验都表明，这种适应性使蠕虫能够钻入许多不同类型的设备中。当黑客从远处释放人工智能时，他们会协调模型的行为。假设一种能够广泛复制自身的人工智能蠕虫可以逃脱任何人的控制。

paras.en: Still, there’s a caveat to the experiments’ results, says Michael Alexander Riegler, a cybersecurity researcher at Simula Metropolitan Center for Digital Engineering in Oslo, Norway. Both teams’ test environments made it easier for the AI worm to spread than it would be in the real world, says Riegler, who was not involved in either study.
paras.zh: 挪威奥斯陆 Simula 大都会数字工程中心的网络安全研究员迈克尔·亚历山大·里格勒 (Michael Alexander Riegler) 表示，实验结果仍然有一个警告。没有参与这两项研究的里格勒表示，两个团队的测试环境都使人工智能蠕虫病毒比在现实世界中更容易传播。

paras.en: And there’s another practical obstacle to the unleashing of AI worms. They use more computing power and take up more space than a conventional worm. The Mirai worm, which took down a slew of websites including Reddit and Spotify in 2016, was a few kilobytes in size, while the medium-sized AI models in the experiments were tens of gigabytes. That’s still way smaller than the massive, top-of-the-line models behind the “rogue AI” incidents that made headlines earlier in 2026. (And those weren’t worms, because they didn’t copy themselves and spread.)
paras.zh: 人工智能蠕虫的释放还有另一个实际障碍。与传统蠕虫相比，它们使用更多的计算能力并占用更多的空间。 Mirai 蠕虫病毒在 2016 年摧毁了包括 Reddit 和 Spotify 在内的一系列网站，其大小只有几千字节，而实验中的中型 AI 模型则有数十 GB。这仍然比 2026 年初成为头条新闻的“流氓人工智能”事件背后的大规模顶级模型要小得多。（这些不是蠕虫病毒，因为它们不会自我复制和传播。）

paras.en: Most devices — including typical laptop computers — don’t have enough space or the right kind of chips to run worm-capable AI models, Guan says. But new versions of devices, such as security cameras, are coming out with advanced hardware for running AI, researchers at the AI company Anthropic write. And at the same time, even smaller AI models are becoming more capable of sophisticated cyberattacks. These developments could expand the pool of devices an AI worm could exploit.
paras.zh: 关说，大多数设备——包括典型的笔记本电脑——没有足够的空间或合适的芯片来运行具有蠕虫能力的人工智能模型。但人工智能公司 Anthropic 的研究人员写道，新版本的设备（例如安全摄像头）正在推出，配备了运行人工智能的先进硬件。与此同时，更小的人工智能模型也变得更有能力进行复杂的网络攻击。这些发展可以扩大人工智能蠕虫可以利用的设备池。

paras.en: “The ingredients are converging” to make AI worms more realistic, Riegler says. How quickly they will converge is up for debate. Anthropic puts the timeline at months into the future, but both Riegler and Guan say it will probably take longer.
paras.zh: 里格勒说，“各种成分正在融合”，使人工智能蠕虫变得更加真实。他们会以多快的速度融合还有待讨论。 Anthropic 将时间表推迟了几个月，但里格勒和关都表示可能需要更长的时间。

paras.en: The Mirai worm spread itself through smart devices including home routers, security cameras and even baby monitors. It broke into these devices by trying a small set of common default usernames and passwords. “Just using this very simple technique, this Mirai botnet was able to infect hundreds of thousands of devices,” says cybersecurity expert Zane Ma of Oregon State University in Corvallis, who presented an analysis of the attack at a 2017 security symposium. High-profile downed sites such as Reddit were actually collateral damage: A small group of young hackers had created the worm to mess with gaming servers.
paras.zh: Mirai 蠕虫通过家庭路由器、安全摄像头甚至婴儿监视器等智能设备进行传播。它通过尝试一小组常见的默认用户名和密码来侵入这些设备。 “仅使用这种非常简单的技术，这个 Mirai 僵尸网络就能够感染数十万台设备，”科瓦利斯俄勒冈州立大学的网络安全专家 Zane Ma 说道，他在 2017 年的安全研讨会上对此次攻击进行了分析。 Reddit 等备受瞩目的网站被关闭实际上是附带损害：一小群年轻的黑客创建了蠕虫病毒来扰乱游戏服务器。

paras.en: Rebooting an infected device cleared Mirai. Changing its default login credentials prevented reinfection through the same route. But an AI-powered worm might make cleaning up this type of cybersecurity breach much more difficult. Why? Because the AI worm acts more like an octopus, Guan says.
paras.zh: 重新启动受感染的设备可清除 Mirai。更改其默认登录凭据可防止通过同一途径再次感染。但人工智能驱动的蠕虫可能会使清理此类网络安全漏洞变得更加困难。为什么？关说，因为人工智能蠕虫的行为更像章鱼。

paras.en: Guan and colleagues tested this octopus-worm in a virtual network. Anchored by several powerful computers that each had a chip called a graphics processing unit, or GPU, the faux networks also contained simulations of smart devices, including office printers and security cameras.
paras.zh: 关和同事在虚拟网络中测试了这种章鱼蠕虫。这些人造网络以几台功能强大的计算机为基础，每台计算机都有一个称为图形处理单元（GPU）的芯片，还包含智能设备的模拟，包括办公室打印机和安全摄像头。

paras.en: The octopus’s AI model head started on a single machine with a GPU. From there it sent out tentacles to take control of smaller devices. Upon encountering a new device, the head would use AI to plan how its tentacle could hack in. Often, a hack wouldn’t work, but the octopus wouldn’t give up. It would use info about how it failed to come up with a new hack to try. That ability is “a new, hypercharged way of attacking systems,” Riegler says. Whenever it found a computer with a large enough GPU, it would copy its head onto that new machine.
paras.zh: 章鱼的人工智能模型头是在一台带有 GPU 的机器上启动的。它从那里伸出触手来控制较小的设备。当遇到新设备时，章鱼的头部会使用人工智能来计划其触手如何侵入。通常，侵入是行不通的，但章鱼不会放弃。它将使用有关它如何未能提出新的黑客尝试的信息。里格勒说，这种能力是“一种新的、强大的系统攻击方式”。每当它发现一台具有足够大 GPU 的计算机时，它就会将其头部复制到该新计算机上。

paras.en: An attacker would probably launch an octopus-style AI worm from the cloud. Click through this slideshow to see how it might spread autonomously. First, it takes over and copies itself onto a device with the right kind of hardware (chip icon) to house an AI model (first image). From there, it sends out tentacles (red arrows) to hack into any connected devices, like 3-D printers and security cameras (second image). Devices that don’t have enough space for the AI model become jumping-off points for the octopus-worm to discover new places to copy itself (third image).
paras.zh: 攻击者可能会从云端启动章鱼式人工智能蠕虫。点击这张幻灯片，看看它如何自动传播。首先，它接管并将自身复制到具有正确类型硬件（芯片图标）的设备上以容纳人工智能模型（第一张图片）。从那里，它会发出触手（红色箭头）来侵入任何连接的设备，例如 3D 打印机和安全摄像头（第二张图片）。没有足够空间容纳人工智能模型的设备成为章鱼蠕虫发现新位置来复制自身的起点（第三张图片）。

paras.en: The head could also search a simulated internet for information about newly discovered vulnerabilities. (The team didn’t connect it to the real internet for obvious reasons — protection against an AI octopus invasion — and spent considerable effort making sure their creation couldn’t escape the lab, Guan says.)
paras.zh: 该负责人还可以在模拟互联网上搜索有关新发现的漏洞的信息。 （关说，出于显而易见的原因，该团队没有将其连接到真正的互联网——防止人工智能章鱼入侵——并花了相当大的努力来确保他们的创造物无法逃出实验室。）

paras.en: The octopus-worm even came up with a way to survive a reboot, something Guan says they hadn’t asked it to do. The team posted a preprint of their findings at arXiv.org on June 2, and the paper is now going through peer review.
paras.zh: 章鱼蠕虫甚至想出了一种在重启后生存的方法，关说他们并没有要求它这样做。该团队于 6 月 2 日在 arXiv.org 上发布了他们的研究结果预印本，该论文目前正在接受同行评审。

paras.en: Meanwhile, at Anthropic, researchers showed another way an AI worm might work by building on Guan and his colleagues’ research. If an octopus-worm wasn’t weird enough, Anthropic dubbed its creation a “digital slime mold”, a name that captures the model’s slow, oozing behavior. Anthropic declined to comment for this story, but Guan says the company’s work shows that “unlike human reasoning, AI reasoning can be distributed.” That means an AI worm wouldn’t necessarily need to hijack a powerful computer to copy and run itself — it could spread its “thinking” out among smaller devices.
paras.zh: 与此同时，在 Anthropic，研究人员在关及其同事的研究基础上展示了人工智能蠕虫的另一种工作方式。如果章鱼蠕虫还不够奇怪的话，Anthropic 将其创造物称为“数字粘液霉菌”，这个名字反映了该模型缓慢、渗出的行为。 Anthropic 拒绝对此事发表评论，但关表示，该公司的工作表明“与人类推理不同，人工智能推理可以是分布式的”。这意味着人工智能蠕虫不一定需要劫持一台功能强大的计算机来复制和运行自己——它可以将其“思维”传播到较小的设备上。

paras.en: And that’s exactly what the slime mold version of an AI worm does. It breaks itself up and runs pieces of the model on multiple smaller devices. In their report posted online October 12, the Anthropic researchers used 15 Android smart TVs that they had networked together.
paras.zh: 这正是人工智能蠕虫的粘菌版本所做的事情。它会自行分解并在多个较小的设备上运行模型的各个部分。在 10 月 12 日在线发布的报告中，Anthropic 研究人员使用了 15 台联网的 Android 智能电视。

paras.en: Anthropic’s chopped-up model processes data thousands of times more slowly than what’s possible with GPUs similar to the ones Guan and colleagues relied on. That’s because the model’s data has to travel over internet connections that could take it all around the world during processing, rather than remaining in one place, within chips optimized for AI processing. That pace was too slow to demonstrate an ability to spread like a computer worm, Guan notes. So the Anthropic team ran a separate experiment with an AI worm running on GPUs that showed it could spread and adapt its attacks to different kinds of devices.
paras.zh: Anthropic 的分割模型处理数据的速度比关及其同事所依赖的 GPU 慢数千倍。这是因为该模型的数据必须通过互联网连接传输，在处理过程中可以将其传送到世界各地，而不是保留在针对人工智能处理优化的芯片内的一个地方。关指出，这种速度太慢，不足以证明其像计算机蠕虫一样传播的能力。因此，Anthropic 团队对在 GPU 上运行的 AI 蠕虫进行了一项单独的实验，结果表明它可以传播并使其攻击适应不同类型的设备。

paras.en: Whether AI worms are coming in months or whether we have longer to prepare, defenders should get ready now, Guan says. And AI worms do have weaknesses.
paras.zh: 关说，无论人工智能蠕虫会在几个月后出现，还是我们需要更长的时间来准备，防御者现在就应该做好准备。人工智能蠕虫确实有弱点。

paras.en: For one thing, the large size of an AI worm could be its downfall. Even if smaller AI models become more capable, these are still big programs that guzzle computing power. You might not notice if your fridge or microwave suddenly started sending lots of traffic onto the network, but your internet service provider would. They’d realize “there’s something weird going on on these devices,” Ma says. From there, they could quarantine affected devices, disconnecting them from the internet to prevent further spread.
paras.zh: 一方面，人工智能蠕虫的巨大尺寸可能是其失败的原因。即使较小的人工智能模型变得更加强大，这些仍然是消耗计算能力的大型程序。您可能不会注意到您的冰箱或微波炉是否突然开始向网络发送大量流量，但您的互联网服务提供商会注意到。马云说，他们会意识到“这些设备上发生了一些奇怪的事情”。从那里，他们可以隔离受影响的设备，断开它们与互联网的连接，以防止进一步传播。

paras.en: Ma also points out that most smart devices in a person’s home aren’t directly connected to the public internet. Most home networks use a router as a central hub, and that provides a layer of protection against a worm attack.
paras.zh: 马云还指出，家庭中的大多数智能设备都没有直接连接到公共互联网。大多数家庭网络使用路由器作为中央集线器，这提供了一层针对蠕虫攻击的保护。

paras.en: Strong passwords, regular updates and other normal security measures would also protect against the attacks demonstrated in both experiments, Riegler says.
paras.zh: 里格勒说，强密码、定期更新和其他正常的安全措施也可以防止这两个实验中展示的攻击。

paras.en: Guan and some colleagues are now testing specific defenses to stop AI worms, including devising an AI-driven defender. Trying to anticipate emerging threats and protect systems ahead of time is “what I’m passionate about,” Guan says. “We are working on the problem day and night.”
paras.zh: 关和一些同事现在正在测试阻止人工智能蠕虫的特定防御措施，包括设计人工智能驱动的防御程序。关说，尝试提前预测新出现的威胁并保护系统是“我热衷的事情”。 “我们正在夜以继日地解决这个问题。”

articles.title: What the Trump administration’s focus on AI and quantum means for science
articles.author: Emily Conover

paras.en: Many fields of science have struggled under the second Trump administration, with funding cuts and delays plaguing research in fields such as public health and climate science. But some topics have found firmer footing, including artificial intelligence and quantum science.
paras.zh: 在特朗普第二届政府领导下，许多科学领域都陷入困境，公共卫生和气候科学等领域的研究受到资金削减和延误的困扰。但一些话题已经找到了更坚实的基础，包括人工智能和量子科学。

paras.en: These technologies, along with supercomputing, “are going to be the three legs of the stool that is going to transform how science and engineering is done,” says Darío Gil, undersecretary for science at the U.S. Department of Energy.
paras.zh: 美国能源部负责科学事务的副部长达里奥·吉尔 (Darío Gil) 表示，这些技术与超级计算“将成为改变科学和工程实施方式的三条腿”。

paras.en: In November 2025, President Donald Trump issued an executive order to launch the Genesis Mission, a $5 billion whole-of-government effort to advance science via artificial intelligence. The initiative began with the DOE but has since expanded to more than 15 federal agencies.
paras.zh: 2025 年 11 月，唐纳德·特朗普总统发布行政命令，启动“创世纪任务”，这是一项耗资 50 亿美元的政府整体计划，旨在通过人工智能推进科学发展。该倡议始于美国能源部，但后来扩展到超过 15 个联邦机构。

paras.en: In June, the president issued an executive order that aims to accelerate the development of tools such as quantum computers, quantum sensors and quantum networks. And in July, the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy issued a 123-page report describing its vision for a “golden age” of federal science, in which agencies align investments in research and development with administration priorities.
paras.zh: 6月，总统发布了一项行政命令，旨在加速量子计算机、量子传感器和量子网络等工具的开发。 7 月，白宫科学技术政策办公室发布了一份 123 页的报告，描述了其对联邦科学“黄金时代”的愿景，其中各机构将研发投资与政府优先事项结合起来。

paras.en: Federal agencies spent some $4.2 billion on AI R&D in 2025, according to an arm of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy that quantifies such investments.
paras.zh: 根据白宫科学技术政策办公室量化此类投资的部门的数据，联邦机构到 2025 年将在人工智能研发上花费约 42 亿美元。

paras.en: Many scientists are enthusiastic about the opportunities for AI and quantum research. But some caution that a measured approach is needed. “My strongest opinion … is that I want to see all fields of science supported,” says Brad Marston, a physicist at Brown University and president of the American Physical Society. “Priorities have to be chosen, but getting a good balance is important, because you never know where some advance will come from.”
paras.zh: 许多科学家对人工智能和量子研究的机会充满热情。但一些人警告说，需要采取谨慎的方法。 “我最强烈的观点……是我希望看到所有科学领域都得到支持，”布朗大学物理学家、美国物理学会主席布拉德·马斯顿说。 “必须选择优先事项，但取得良好的平衡很重要，因为你永远不知道一些进展将从何而来。”

paras.en: Through Genesis, the DOE plans to use its troves of data as well as experimental and computing facilities to produce a common set of AI tools and a shared ecosystem for science. “That’s conceptually a very powerful idea,” says astronomer Rachel Mandelbaum of Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh. “And if it pans out as intended, it could drive great advances in science and technology.”
paras.zh: 通过 Genesis，美国能源部计划利用其大量数据以及实验和计算设施来生产一套通用的人工智能工具和一个共享的科学生态系统。 “从概念上讲，这是一个非常强大的想法，”匹兹堡卡内基梅隆大学的天文学家雷切尔·曼德尔鲍姆说。 “如果它如预期那样成功，它将推动科学技术的巨大进步。”

paras.en: This year, DOE funded nearly 300 projects through Genesis — including one led by Mandelbaum. Her team’s effort aims to unify immense datasets from astronomical facilities around the world, such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument and the Zwicky Transient Facility. That would enable AI models to be trained on the data, which could help uncover hidden astronomical insights.
paras.zh: 今年，能源部通过 Genesis 资助了近 300 个项目，其中包括曼德尔鲍姆领导的一个项目。她的团队致力于统一来自世界各地天文设施的海量数据集，例如维拉·C·鲁宾天文台、暗能量光谱仪和兹威基瞬态设施。这将使人工智能模型能够根据数据进行训练，这有助于揭示隐藏的天文见解。

paras.en: Other projects include efforts to accelerate nuclear reactor development, create simulations of the U.S. electric grid and study nuclear fusion. And federal agencies including the National Science Foundation and the National Institutes of Health have launched their own Genesis efforts, centered around the mission’s National Science and Technology Challenges, which include topics in health, biology, energy, space, national security and more.
paras.zh: 其他项目包括加速核反应堆开发、创建美国电网模拟以及研究核聚变。美国国家科学基金会和美国国立卫生研究院等联邦机构也启动了自己的创世纪计划，围绕该任务的国家科学和技术挑战，其中包括健康、生物学、能源、太空、国家安全等主题。

paras.en: Many scientists were already wielding AI in their work. But Genesis “really did create an inflection point,” says John Sarrao, director of SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory in Menlo Park, Calif. SLAC is now involved with 20 Genesis projects and leads two.
paras.zh: 许多科学家已经在他们的工作中运用人工智能。但位于加利福尼亚州门洛帕克的 SLAC 国家加速器实验室主任 John Sarrao 表示，Genesis“确实创造了一个拐点”。SLAC 目前参与了 20 个 Genesis 项目，并领导了其中两个项目。

paras.en: Compared with AI, quantum technologies are less mature. With quantum computing, “we’re still at mile one or two or three of a marathon,” says Celia Merzbacher, executive director of the Quantum Economic Development Consortium, a coalition of public and private institutions that works to bolster quantum tech in the United States. Nevertheless, researchers hope the two technologies can amplify one another. AI could help design and develop quantum computers, for example, while quantum computing shows promise for efficiently tackling certain machine learning problems.
paras.zh: 与人工智能相比，量子技术还不太成熟。量子经济发展联盟（Quantum Economic Development Consortium）执行董事西莉亚·梅尔兹巴赫（Celia Merzbacher）表示，对于量子计算，“我们仍处于马拉松比赛的一英里、二英里或三英里处”。该联盟是一个由公共和私人机构组成的联盟，致力于支持美国的量子技术。尽管如此，研究人员希望这两种技术能够相互增强。例如，人工智能可以帮助设计和开发量子计算机，而量子计算有望有效解决某些机器学习问题。

paras.en: Accordingly, several Genesis projects involve quantum error correction, quantum sensors and quantum materials. And the DOE’s Quantum Genesis initiative aims to develop scientifically useful, error-corrected quantum computers by 2028.
paras.zh: 因此，几个 Genesis 项目涉及量子纠错、量子传感器和量子材料。美国能源部的量子创世纪计划旨在到 2028 年开发出具有科学用途、可纠错的量子计算机。

paras.en: AI and quantum were not always hot topics. “Both of those areas … were kind of backwaters until recent advances,” Marston says. Before the development of deep neural networks, for example, AI was mostly a curiosity. “It points to the importance of having a balanced approach to science funding,” he says. What starts as an obscure scientific specialty may suddenly explode into wide relevance.
paras.zh: 人工智能和量子并不总是热门话题。马斯顿说：“在最近取得进展之前，这两个领域都处于停滞状态。”例如，在深度神经网络发展之前，人工智能主要是一种好奇心。 “这表明了科学资助采取平衡方法的重要性，”他说。一开始作为一个默默无闻的科学专业可能会突然爆发出广泛的相关性。

paras.en: In the context of limited resources, prioritizing one area of research necessitates deprioritizing another. While some funding for the DOE’s portion of Genesis came from the One Big Beautiful Bill passed in 2025, much of the rest came from the DOE’s budget.
paras.zh: 在资源有限的情况下，优先考虑一个研究领域就需要降低另一个研究领域的优先顺序。虽然能源部 Genesis 部分的部分资金来自 2025 年通过的《一项美丽的大法案》，但其余大部分来自能源部的预算。

paras.en: As excited as Mandelbaum is about Genesis, she is concerned about funding for non-AI related work. A cosmology grant her group received from the DOE didn’t align with Genesis mission priorities and was reduced this year, she says. “If the reality is that some of this [funding] is coming out of the baseline research budget in my field, then I think that it would be beneficial for the DOE to engage the scientific community about those trade-offs,” Mandelbaum says.
paras.zh: 尽管曼德尔鲍姆对《创世纪》感到兴奋，但她也担心非人工智能相关工作的资金问题。她说，她的团队从美国能源部获得的宇宙学资助与创世纪任务的优先事项不符，今年被减少了。 “如果现实情况是部分[资金]来自我所在领域的基线研究预算，那么我认为能源部让科学界参与这些权衡将是有益的，”曼德尔鲍姆说。

paras.en: In response to these concerns, Gil says that the money going to Genesis from the DOE’s Office of Science — about $400 million so far — is small compared to the office’s total FY2026 budget of $8.4 billion.
paras.zh: 针对这些担忧，吉尔表示，与该办公室 2026 财年 84 亿美元的总预算相比，能源部科学办公室向 Genesis 提供的资金（迄今为止约为 4 亿美元）很小。

paras.en: Sarrao says that it’s important to build on the momentum of Genesis while still supporting the DOE’s core research. His impression is that things are trending in the right direction. “Are there really exciting opportunities? Yes, 100 percent,” Sarrao says. “Are there risks if you get the balance wrong? Equally well, 100 percent.”
paras.zh: Sarrao 表示，在继续支持能源部核心研究的同时，在 Genesis 的发展势头基础上发展非常重要。他的印象是事情正在朝着正确的方向发展。 “真的有令人兴奋的机会吗？是的，100%，”萨拉奥说。 “如果你的平衡错了，会有风险吗？同样好，100%。”

articles.title: NASA's Curiosity Rover Burst Open a Rock on Mars And Found a Big Surprise
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: Even though Mars is millions of kilometers across the Solar System, scientists have a pretty good handle on its geology.
paras.zh: 尽管火星横跨太阳系数百万公里，但科学家们对其地质状况有相当好的了解。

paras.en: We know, broadly, what types of minerals can be found there, and the geological processes that shape it.
paras.zh: 我们广泛地知道那里可以找到什么类型的矿物，以及塑造它的地质过程。

paras.en: But then sometimes all we have to do is scratch the surface, and a whole new mystery comes tumbling out, glinting dully under the Martian Sun.
paras.zh: 但有时我们所要做的只是触及表面，一个全新的谜团就会浮现出来，在火星阳光下暗淡地闪烁。

paras.en: Like the time in 2024 when NASA's Curiosity rover rolled its 899-kilogram (1,982-pound) body over a completely unremarkable rock in the Gale Crater's Gediz Vallis Channel.
paras.zh: 就像 2024 年 NASA 的“好奇号”火星车将其重达 899 公斤（1,982 磅）的机身滚动到盖尔陨石坑盖迪兹山谷通道中一块完全不起眼的岩石上时。

paras.en: When the rock burst open under the strain, the pale yellow shine of its contents stumped NASA scientists – it appeared to be crystals of startlingly pure elemental sulfur – brimstone.
paras.zh: 当岩石在压力下爆裂时，其内容物发出的淡黄色光芒让美国宇航局的科学家们感到困惑——它似乎是纯度惊人的元素硫——硫磺的晶体。

paras.en: Although sulfates are fairly common on Mars, this marked the first time sulfur had been found on the red planet in its pure elemental form – and the surrounding ground was littered with more of the same kind of rock.
paras.zh: 尽管硫酸盐在火星上相当常见，但这标志着首次在这颗红色星球上发现纯元素形式的硫，而周围的地面上散布着更多同类岩石。

paras.en: "Finding a field of stones made of pure sulfur is like finding an oasis in the desert," Curiosity project scientist Ashwin Vasavada of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory said at the time.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局喷气推进实验室的好奇号项目科学家阿什温·瓦萨瓦达当时表示：“找到一块由纯硫制成的石头就像在沙漠中找到绿洲一样。”

paras.en: Sulfates are salts containing sulfur and oxygen, often dissolved in water alongside other minerals. When the water evaporates, sulfate minerals can crystallize out, leaving deposits behind.
paras.zh: 硫酸盐是含有硫和氧的盐，通常与其他矿物质一起溶解在水中。当水蒸发时，硫酸盐矿物质会结晶出来，留下沉积物。

paras.en: These sulfate minerals can tell us a lot about Mars, such as its water history and how it has weathered over time.
paras.zh: 这些硫酸盐矿物质可以告诉我们很多关于火星的信息，例如它的水历史以及它如何随着时间的推移而风化。

paras.en: Pure sulfur is a different matter altogether. On Earth, large deposits are often associated with volcanic or hydrothermal activity, but there was no evidence of the high-temperature conditions that could have produced such a deposit directly in Gediz Vallis.
paras.zh: 纯硫则完全是另一回事。在地球上，大型矿床通常与火山或热液活动有关，但没有证据表明高温条件可以直接在盖迪兹山谷中产生这样的矿床。

paras.en: There are, to be fair, a lot of things we don't know about the geological history of Mars. But finding scads of pure sulfur just hanging about on the Martian surface suggested that something important was missing from our understanding.
paras.zh: 公平地说，关于火星的地质历史，我们还有很多不了解的事情。但在火星表面发现了大量的纯硫表明我们的理解中缺少一些重要的东西。

paras.en: Now, two new studies have begun to piece together how this strange deposit might have formed – and what it could tell us about the ancient Martian environment.
paras.zh: 现在，两项新研究已经开始拼凑出这种奇怪沉积物可能是如何形成的，以及它可以告诉我们有关古代火星环境的信息。

paras.en: In a paper published in Science in June 2026, a team led by planetary scientist Scott VanBommel of Washington University in St. Louis took a closer look at Curiosity's observations of the sulfur-rich rocks, revealing that the discovery was even more unusual than it first appeared.
paras.zh: 在 2026 年 6 月《科学》杂志上发表的一篇论文中，圣路易斯华盛顿大学的行星科学家斯科特·范博梅尔 (Scott VanBommel) 领导的团队仔细研究了好奇号对富含硫岩石的观察结果，发现这一发现比最初出现时更加不寻常。

paras.en: He and his colleagues studied the images the rover had taken of the region, along with its chemical analyses of the sulfur it unmarsed.
paras.zh: 他和他的同事研究了火星车拍摄的该地区的图像，以及对其分解的硫进行的化学分析。

paras.en: The results confirmed that the initial impression of the amount of sulfur was correct. It lay scattered across an area measuring some 2,100 square meters. One pure sulfur rock was weird enough, but this was positively preposterous.
paras.zh: 结果证实了对硫含量的初步印象是正确的。它分散在面积约 2,100 平方米的区域。一块纯硫磺岩石已经够奇怪的了，但这绝对是荒谬的。

paras.en: And it was remarkably pure – a stark contrast to the sulfate minerals usually found on Mars.
paras.zh: 而且它非常纯净——与火星上通常发现的硫酸盐矿物形成鲜明对比。

paras.en: There was one more key piece of information. Curiosity weighs much less on Mars, thanks to the red planet's lower gravity – about as much as a 341-kilogram object weighs on Earth. The way the rock popped open when Curiosity bore down with just some of this weight suggests that it was relatively fragile.
paras.zh: 还有一个关键信息。由于这颗红色行星的重力较低，好奇号在火星上的重量要轻得多——大约相当于地球上 341 公斤重的物体的重量。当“好奇号”仅承受如此重量的一部分时，岩石突然裂开的方式表明它相对脆弱。

paras.en: VanBommel and his colleagues believe that the most plausible way so many fragile rocks could come to be scattered intact in Gediz Vallis is if they formed there.
paras.zh: 范博梅尔和他的同事认为，这么多脆弱的岩石在盖迪兹山谷中完好无损地分散的最可能的方式就是它们在那里形成。

paras.en: One possibility, the researchers suggest, is that the sulfur originated in gases released by ancient volcanic activity. As those gases cooled, they became trapped beneath the Martian surface, possibly within cage-like structures of ice called clathrates.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，一种可能性是硫源自古代火山活动释放的气体。当这些气体冷却时，它们被困在火星表面下方，可能在称为包合物的笼状冰结构内。

paras.en: Over time, erosion carved out Gediz Vallis, releasing pressure on the buried gases and allowing them to escape. Chemical reactions between the sulfur-bearing gases could then have produced deposits of pure sulfur, without the need for high temperatures at the site.
paras.zh: 随着时间的推移，侵蚀侵蚀了盖迪兹山谷，释放了埋藏气体的压力，使它们得以逸出。含硫气体之间的化学反应可能会产生纯硫沉积物，而无需现场高温。

paras.en: Based on the geological context, the researchers estimate that the sulfur deposit formed between 3.1 and 2.8 billion years ago.
paras.zh: 根据地质背景，研究人员估计硫矿床形成于 3.1 至 28 亿年前。

paras.en: "It's hard to wrap your head around how long those rocks had been sitting there with little to no chemical alteration happening to them," geochemist Jeff Berger of NASA's Johnson Space Center, who co-led the study, said.
paras.zh: 这项研究的共同领导者、美国宇航局约翰逊航天中心的地球化学家杰夫·伯杰说：“很难想象这些岩石在那里放置了多久，几乎没有发生任何化学变化。”

paras.en: But this is not the only way elemental sulfur could have formed on Mars.
paras.zh: 但这并不是元素硫在火星上形成的唯一方式。

paras.en: In a separate study published in Geophysical Research Letters in July 2026, atmospheric scientist Jiawei Wang of Cornell University led a team that investigated whether a chemical reaction in water could produce pure sulfur without high temperatures or the involvement of living organisms.
paras.zh: 在 2026 年 7 月《地球物理研究快报》上发表的另一项研究中，康奈尔大学的大气科学家 Jiawei Wang 领导的一个团队研究了水中的化学反应是否可以在没有高温或生物体参与的情况下产生纯硫。

paras.en: The researchers mixed dissolved sulfide with chlorate, a compound containing chlorine and oxygen that may have been present on ancient Mars, in acidic water at room temperature.
paras.zh: 研究人员将溶解的硫化物与氯酸盐（一种可能存在于古代火星上的含有氯和氧的化合物）在室温下的酸性水中混合。

paras.en: And sure enough, the reaction produced tiny yellow crystals of elemental sulfur.
paras.zh: 果然，反应产生了微小的黄色单质硫晶体。

paras.en: Crucially, the amount of chlorate made a significant difference – lower concentrations favored the formation of pure sulfur, while higher concentrations produced more sulfate.
paras.zh: 至关重要的是，氯酸盐的含量产生了显着的差异——较低的浓度有利于纯硫的形成，而较高的浓度则产生更多的硫酸盐。

paras.en: The crystals were microscopic, rather than the chunks Curiosity encountered, but the researchers suggest that similar reactions occurring over much longer periods could produce larger deposits.
paras.zh: 这些晶体是微观的，而不是好奇号遇到的块状晶体，但研究人员认为，在更长的时间内发生的类似反应可能会产生更大的沉积物。

paras.en: And Wang's team noted that the hydrogen sulfide needed for the reaction could have come from the same underground gas reservoirs proposed by VanBommel's team.
paras.zh: 王的团队指出，反应所需的硫化氢可能来自范博梅尔团队提出的同一地下气藏。

paras.en: But why so much fuss about yellow rocks on a red world?
paras.zh: 但为什么对红色世界上的黄色岩石如此大惊小怪呢？

paras.en: Sulfur, it's important to understand, is an essential element for all life. Many organisms take it up in the form of sulfates, using it to make two of the amino acids essential for building proteins.
paras.zh: 重要的是要了解硫是所有生命的必需元素。许多生物体以硫酸盐的形式吸收它，用它来制造构建蛋白质所必需的两种氨基酸。

paras.en: Since we've known about sulfates on Mars for some time, the discovery doesn't tell us anything new in that area. And although microbes can produce elemental sulfur here on Earth, Wang's experiments show that living organisms aren't necessary to explain how it might have formed on Mars.
paras.zh: 由于我们对火星上的硫酸盐了解已有一段时间，这一发现并没有告诉我们该领域的任何新内容。尽管微生物可以在地球上产生元素硫，但王的实验表明，没有必要用活生物体来解释它在火星上是如何形成的。

paras.en: We're yet to find any conclusive signs of life on Mars, anyway. But we do keep stumbling across bits and pieces that living organisms would find useful, including chemistry, water, and past habitable conditions.
paras.zh: 无论如何，我们还没有在火星上发现任何确凿的生命迹象。但我们确实不断地偶然发现对生物体有用的点点滴滴，包括化学、水和过去的宜居条件。

paras.en: It's interesting that the stuff life needs keeps turning up on a planet that – so far at least – seems utterly devoid of it.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，生命所需的物质不断出现在一个——至少到目前为止——似乎完全缺乏的星球上。

paras.en: Because once upon a time, Earth, too, was devoid of life. The two planets have taken different paths, but what we find on Mars could contain tantalizing clues to how our own world evolved, long, long ago.
paras.zh: 因为从前，地球也没有生命。这两颗行星走了不同的道路，但我们在火星上发现的东西可能包含着关于我们自己的世界在很久很久以前是如何演化的诱人线索。

paras.en: "Mars provides us with a frozen snapshot from billions of years ago," Berger said. "We can go back and look at deep time in a way that we can't do on Earth."
paras.zh: “火星为我们提供了数十亿年前的冷冻快照，”伯杰说。 “我们可以回去以一种我们在地球上无法做到的方式来观察深层时间。”

paras.en: The two papers were published in Science and Geophysical Research Letters.
paras.zh: 这两篇论文发表在《科学》和《地球物理研究快报》上。

articles.title: The World's First 'Dark Magic Mushroom' Is Hiding a Potentially Deadly Secret
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: The mushrooms of the world are a decidedly mixed bag, but one thing's for sure: You don't want to get them confused.
paras.zh: 世界上的蘑菇绝对是鱼龙混杂，但有一件事是肯定的：你不想让它们混淆。

paras.en: Far from the familiarity of grocery store varieties, if you go down in the woods today, mushrooms take a wild turn.
paras.zh: 与杂货店里熟悉的品种截然不同，如果你今天走进树林，蘑菇就会发生疯狂的转变。

paras.en: While some wild mushrooms are edible, many are not safe to eat.
paras.zh: 虽然一些野生蘑菇可以食用，但许多野生蘑菇并不安全。

paras.en: Hundreds of different kinds are poisonous, and some are deadly – most notoriously, the world's deadliest mushroom: the 'death cap' (Amanita phalloides).
paras.zh: 数百种不同的蘑菇都是有毒的，有些甚至是致命的——其中最臭名昭著的是世界上最致命的蘑菇：“死亡帽”（Amanita phalloides）。

paras.en: But toxic mushrooms are only one side of the story. Nature also abounds with psychedelic mushrooms – aka 'magic mushrooms' – which have evolved hallucinogenic substances.
paras.zh: 但有毒蘑菇只是故事的一方面。自然界还盛产迷幻蘑菇——又名“魔法蘑菇”——它们进化出了致幻物质。

paras.en: Until recently, scientists had never seen a mushroom that sat in both these camps, producing both psilocybin, the main psychedelic compound in magic mushrooms, and the toxins that make death caps so deadly.
paras.zh: 直到最近，科学家们还从未见过这两个营地中存在一种蘑菇，它既能产生裸盖菇素（迷幻蘑菇中的主要迷幻化合物），又能产生使死帽菌如此致命的毒素。

paras.en: But in a new study, researchers report the identification of the world's first "dark magic mushroom" – a mysterious fungus that contains both psychedelic chemicals and poisonous amatoxins, described in Current Biology.
paras.zh: 但在一项新的研究中，研究人员报告了世界上第一个“黑暗魔法蘑菇”的鉴定，这是一种神秘的真菌，含有致幻化学物质和有毒的鹅膏毒素，《当代生物学》中对此进行了描述。

paras.en: "We matched up our findings and confirmed that we saw both compounds," says fungal biologist Andrew Kunik from Harvard University, who completed the research while studying at the University of Florida.
paras.zh: 哈佛大学真菌生物学家安德鲁·库尼克（Andrew Kunik）在佛罗里达大学学习期间完成了这项研究，他说：“我们对我们的发现进行了匹配，并确认我们看到了这两种化合物。”

paras.en: "I could hardly believe it. We knew it was possible but tried not to get too excited until we did a more rigorous analysis."
paras.zh: “我简直不敢相信。我们知道这是可能的，但在我们进行更严格的分析之前，我们尽量不要太兴奋。”

paras.en: The species in question – called Galerina indica – was first discovered in India over a decade ago.
paras.zh: 这种被称为 Galerina indica 的物种是十多年前在印度首次发现的。

paras.en: But it wasn't until Kunik and team closely investigated G. indica specimens found clinging to a moss-covered palm trunk in Florida's wetlands that researchers realized how uniquely devilish this strange mushroom really is.
paras.zh: 但直到库尼克和他的团队仔细研究了在佛罗里达州湿地发现的粘在长满青苔的棕榈树干上的印度蘑菇标本后，研究人员才意识到这种奇怪的蘑菇到底有多么独特和邪恶。

paras.en: While the infamous death cap (from the Amanita genus) grabs most of the headlines, the world's first dark magic mushroom hails from another deadly collective.
paras.zh: 虽然臭名昭著的死亡帽（来自鹅膏菌属）占据了大部分头条新闻，但世界上第一个黑魔法蘑菇却来自另一个致命的群体。

paras.en: G. indica belongs to the Galerina genus and is related to a poisonous group of mushrooms known as the Galerina marginata species complex, commonly known as 'funeral bells' and 'deadly skullcaps', among other well-deserved handles.
paras.zh: G. indica 属于 Galerina 属，与一种被称为 Galerina marginata 物种复合体的有毒蘑菇有亲缘关系，通常被称为“葬礼钟声”和“致命黄芩”等当之无愧的手柄。

paras.en: Exactly why G. indica branched out from the family business of poisoning into a psychedelic side hustle remains unclear. But the same mystery basically surrounds all magic mushrooms.
paras.zh: 究竟为什么 G. indica 会从家族投毒生意转向迷幻副业，目前还不清楚。但同样的谜团基本上围绕着所有的迷幻蘑菇。

paras.en: "We still don't fully understand why mushrooms produce psilocybin," Kunik says.
paras.zh: “我们仍然不完全理解为什么蘑菇会产生裸盖菇素，”库尼克说。

paras.en: "Amatoxins may help protect mushrooms from animals that eat them, but their precise ecological role isn't entirely clear either. That's what makes the discovery of the 'dark magic mushroom' so interesting. Why would a mushroom produce both of these compounds, and what advantage might that give it in nature?"
paras.zh: “鹅膏毒素可能有助于保护蘑菇免受动物食用，但它们确切的生态作用也不完全清楚。这就是‘黑魔法蘑菇’的发现如此有趣的原因。为什么蘑菇会产生这两种化合物，这会给它在自然界带来什么优势？”

paras.en: While we don't have all the answers, we are slowly learning some of the backstory.
paras.zh: 虽然我们没有所有的答案，但我们正在慢慢了解一些背景故事。

paras.en: In the study, the researchers chemically analyzed their G. indica specimens, as well as sequencing the species' genome.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，研究人员对 G. indica 标本进行了化学分析，并对该物种的基因组进行了测序。

paras.en: While mushroom-forming fungal species usually inherit the genes responsible for producing specialized chemicals from their ancestors, G. indica's double whammy appears to be an incredibly rare instance of two separate cases of horizontal gene transfer involving the Galerina genus, in which genes were transferred between organisms rather than passed down from parents to offspring.
paras.zh: 虽然形成蘑菇的真菌物种通常从其祖先那里继承了负责产生特殊化学物质的基因，但印度蘑菇的双重打击似乎是涉及 Galerina 属的两个独立的水平基因转移案例中极其罕见的例子，其中基因在生物体之间转移，而不是从亲本传给后代。

paras.en: "Horizontal gene transfer is like if we shook hands and some of my DNA incorporated into your genome," says co-author and mycologist Bryn Dentinger from the University of Utah.
paras.zh: 犹他大学的合著者、真菌学家 Bryn Dentinger 表示：“水平基因转移就像我们握手时，我的一些 DNA 就会融入到你的基因组中。”

paras.en: "Two independent horizontal gene transfer events for these specialized metabolites in one mushroom genus are unheard of."
paras.zh: “在一个蘑菇属中，这些特殊代谢物发生两次独立的水平基因转移事件是闻所未闻的。”

paras.en: In this case, the researchers think it's most likely that an ancestor of G. indica, already capable of producing amatoxins, acquired the genes for making psilocybin through horizontal gene transfer. A separate Galerina lineage appears to have independently acquired those same capabilities.
paras.zh: 在这种情况下，研究人员认为很可能是已经能够产生鹅膏毒素的G. indica的祖先通过水平基因转移获得了制造裸盖菇素的基因。一个单独的加莱里纳血统似乎独立地获得了这些相同的能力。

paras.en: It remains unknown why it would benefit G. indica to produce both toxic and psychedelic compounds, but the researchers say it may represent an example of a diversified defense strategy, in which distinct combinations of toxic compounds might help to slow down or deter animals feeding on the fungi.
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚为什么 G. indica 产生有毒和致幻化合物对 G. indica 有利，但研究人员表示，这可能代表了多样化防御策略的一个例子，其中有毒化合物的不同组合可能有助于减缓或阻止动物以真菌为食。

paras.en: While it's not yet clear from this study whether the amounts of toxins in G. indica are dangerous or deadly to humans, the researchers warn that the mushroom does develop blue bruising when handled – a phenomenon linked to psilocybin in mushrooms.
paras.zh: 虽然这项研究尚不清楚G. indica中的毒素含量对人类是否危险或致命，但研究人员警告说，这种蘑菇在处理时确实会出现蓝色瘀伤，这种现象与蘑菇中的裸盖菇素有关。

paras.en: Before now, some foragers might have assumed those blue marks meant it was safe to consume – containing psilocybin instead of poisonous amatoxins – but the existence of G. indica suggests some mushrooms aren't so easily pigeonholed.
paras.zh: 在此之前，一些采摘者可能认为这些蓝色标记意味着可以安全食用——含有裸盖菇素而不是有毒的鹅膏毒素——但印度蘑菇的存在表明一些蘑菇并不那么容易被归类。

paras.en: "From a public-health perspective, our finding cautions against interpreting blue bruising as evidence that an uncharacterized psiloid-containing mushroom is free of amatoxins," the researchers write in their paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在论文中写道：“从公共卫生的角度来看，我们的发现警告不要将蓝色瘀伤解释为未表征的含赛螺蘑菇不含鹅膏毒素的证据。”

paras.en: "Indeed, we show that this blueing reaction can accompany amatoxins in some rare and uncharacterized species, as is the case for the 'dark magic mushroom' G. indica."
paras.zh: “事实上，我们表明，在一些稀有和未表征的物种中，这种蓝化反应可能伴随着鹅膏毒素，就像‘黑魔法蘑菇’G. indica 的情况一样。”

paras.en: The findings are reported in Current Biology.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《当代生物学》杂志上。

articles.title: A Gene Inherited From Neanderthals Is Still Shaping Human Brains – And May Affect Schizophrenia Risk
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: Tens of thousands of years ago, the last Neanderthal disappeared from our world.
paras.zh: 数万年前，最后一个尼安德特人从我们的世界消失了。

paras.en: But the ghost of this ancient human relative lives on – its lingering traces haunting the Homo sapiens genetic code.
paras.zh: 但这个远古人类亲戚的幽灵依然存在——它挥之不去的痕迹困扰着智人的遗传密码。

paras.en: It manifests in some curious ways – certain hair textures, for example, or how the body stores fat, may be influenced by DNA inherited from ancestors that mingled with their Neanderthal neighbors.
paras.zh: 它以一些奇怪的方式表现出来——例如，某些头发的质地，或者身体储存脂肪的方式，可能会受到从与尼安德特人邻居混居的祖先那里继承的 DNA 的影响。

paras.en: That inheritance may be shaping more than what we look like. A new study has found a tiny stretch of Neanderthal DNA associated with a measurable difference in the size of the occipital lobes – the region that occupies the back of the brain.
paras.zh: 这种遗传所塑造的可能不仅仅是我们的外表。一项新研究发现，一小段尼安德特人 DNA 与枕叶（位于大脑后部的区域）大小的可测量差异相关。

paras.en: And intriguingly, the same genetic variant is also linked to a slightly lower risk of schizophrenia – but no association with general cognitive ability.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，相同的基因变异也与略低的精神分裂症风险有关，但与一般认知能力无关。

paras.en: "Differences in the occipital region of the brain between Neanderthals and modern humans have long been inferred from the fossil record," write anthropologists Hugo Zeberg and Svante Pääbo of the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in a paper published in PNAS.
paras.zh: 马克斯·普朗克进化人类学研究所的人类学家 Hugo Zeberg 和 Svante Pääbo 在《美国国家科学院院刊》上发表的一篇论文中写道：“长期以来，人们从化石记录中推断出尼安德特人与现代人类大脑枕叶区的差异。”

paras.en: "Here, we show that a common genetic variant influencing occipital brain volume in present-day people was inherited from Neanderthals."
paras.zh: “在这里，我们发现影响现代人枕叶脑容量的常见遗传变异是从尼安德特人遗传的。”

paras.en: History used to paint Neanderthals as closer to apes than humans in terms of cognitive ability; more recently, anthropologists have begun to discover that our hominid cousins may have had complex social and symbolic lives, artistic abilities, engineering ingenuity, and other traits once considered uniquely human.
paras.zh: 历史曾将尼安德特人的认知能力描述为比人类更接近猿类。最近，人类学家开始发现，我们的原始人类表亲可能拥有复杂的社会和象征生活、艺术能力、工程独创性以及曾经被认为是人类独有的其他特征。

paras.en: Likewise, too, their brains were not small. In fact, they were comparable in size to the brains of modern humans – sometimes even larger.
paras.zh: 同样，他们的大脑也不小。事实上，它们的大小与现代人类的大脑相当，有时甚至更大。

paras.en: Where they differed was in shape. The skulls of modern humans are relatively rounded, or globular; Neanderthal skulls were more elongated, extending farther from front to back.
paras.zh: 它们的不同之处在于形状。现代人类的头骨相对圆形或球状；尼安德特人的头骨更长，从前到后延伸得更远。

paras.en: This suggests that, although our brains were similar in overall size, the tissue inside may have been distributed differently.
paras.zh: 这表明，尽管我们的大脑总体大小相似，但内部组织的分布可能不同。

paras.en: One region of particular interest is the occipital lobe, which sits at the back of the brain and contains the visual cortex, responsible for processing information received from the eyes (yes, you 'see' things in the back of your head).
paras.zh: 一个特别令人感兴趣的区域是枕叶，它位于大脑后部，包含视觉皮层，负责处理从眼睛接收到的信息（是的，你在后脑勺“看到”东西）。

paras.en: Previous research examining the internal shapes of fossil skulls suggests that Neanderthals may have had proportionally larger occipital lobes than modern humans.
paras.zh: 先前对化石头骨内部形状的研究表明，尼安德特人的枕叶可能比现代人的比例更大。

paras.en: But fossil skulls can only tell us so much about the soft tissue they once contained. To learn more about the evolutionary history of our brains, scientists need to look deeper – into the genetic instructions that help build them in the first place.
paras.zh: 但头骨化石只能告诉我们很多关于它们曾经包含的软组织的信息。为了更多地了解我们大脑的进化史，科学家们需要更深入地研究帮助构建大脑的遗传指令。

paras.en: This is where Zeberg and Pääbo enter the story. They specifically wanted to know whether humans had inherited any Neanderthal genetic variants associated with the size of the occipital lobe.
paras.zh: 这就是泽伯格和帕博进入故事的地方。他们特别想知道人类是否继承了与枕叶大小相关的尼安德特人基因变异。

paras.en: Previous genome studies had identified four locations on the genome of living humans associated with this trait. That was the easy part.
paras.zh: 之前的基因组研究已经确定了人类基因组上与这一特征相关的四个位置。这是最简单的部分。

paras.en: The hard part was showing any of them were related to a long-extinct human ancestor.
paras.zh: 困难的部分是证明它们中的任何一个都与灭绝已久的人类祖先有关。

paras.en: First, the researchers looked at where the four genetic variants appeared in modern human populations.
paras.zh: 首先，研究人员研究了四种遗传变异在现代人类群体中出现的位置。

paras.en: Three were found in populations in sub-Saharan Africa. But the fourth, a tiny deletion of just four DNA letters on chromosome 14, was found only outside that region.
paras.zh: 在撒哈拉以南非洲的人群中发现了三种。但第四个，即 14 号染色体上仅四个 DNA 字母的微小缺失，仅在该区域之外发现。

paras.en: The deletion sits near a gene called DAAM1, which plays a role in brain development. The researchers suspect the inherited DNA may influence how this gene is expressed, potentially helping explain its association with brain structure.
paras.zh: 该缺失位于一个名为 DAAM1 的基因附近，该基因在大脑发育中发挥着重要作用。研究人员怀疑遗传的 DNA 可能会影响该基因的表达方式，从而可能有助于解释其与大脑结构的关联。

paras.en: This was a promising clue. Neanderthals interbred with the ancestors of modern humans after those humans migrated out of Africa.
paras.zh: 这是一个有希望的线索。在现代人类迁出非洲后，尼安德特人与现代人类的祖先杂交。

paras.en: That means traces of their DNA can be found in populations across much of the world – but at significantly lower levels in sub-Saharan Africa, where most ancestors of present-day populations had not encountered Neanderthals.
paras.zh: 这意味着他们的 DNA 痕迹可以在世界大部分地区的人群中找到，但在撒哈拉以南非洲的水平明显较低，那里当今人群的大多数祖先都没有遇到过尼安德特人。

paras.en: The researchers then compared the variant with ancient DNA from five Neanderthals and two Denisovans, another extinct group of ancient humans.
paras.zh: 研究人员随后将这一变体与来自五个尼安德特人和两个丹尼索瓦人（另一个已灭绝的古人类群体）的古代DNA进行了比较。

paras.en: All five Neanderthals carried the deletion. The two Denisovans did not.
paras.zh: 所有五个尼安德特人都携带了该缺失。两个丹尼索瓦人却没有。

paras.en: But this does not mean that the deletion necessarily came from Neanderthals. Another possibility was that both Neanderthals and modern humans inherited it from an even earlier common ancestor.
paras.zh: 但这并不意味着删除一定来自尼安德特人。另一种可能性是，尼安德特人和现代人类都从更早的共同祖先那里继承了它。

paras.en: One way to learn more is by looking at the region of the genome around the variant.
paras.zh: 了解更多信息的一种方法是查看变体周围的基因组区域。

paras.en: Over successive generations, inherited stretches of DNA are gradually broken up and rearranged through a process called recombination – so if the deletion were inherited from a common ancestor hundreds of thousands of years ago, the surrounding DNA should be much more fragmented.
paras.zh: 在连续的几代人中，遗传的 DNA 片段逐渐被分解，并通过一个称为重组的过程重新排列——因此，如果缺失是从数十万年前的共同祖先那里遗传下来的，那么周围的 DNA 应该会更加碎片化。

paras.en: The stretch the researchers found was nearly 60,000 DNA letters long – much longer than would be expected if it had been passed down from such a distant ancestor.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现的这段DNA序列有近60,000个DNA字母长——如果它是从如此遥远的祖先那里传承下来的话，这比预期的要长得多。

paras.en: This provided strong evidence that the DNA had entered the modern human genome much more recently, through interbreeding with Neanderthals.
paras.zh: 这提供了强有力的证据，证明 DNA 是在最近通过与尼安德特人的杂交进入现代人类基因组的。

paras.en: "We were particularly surprised that the genetic variant most strongly associated with the volume of this part of the occipital lobe was inherited from Neanderthals," Zeberg told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 泽伯格告诉《ScienceAlert》：“我们特别惊讶的是，与这部分枕叶体积最密切相关的遗传变异是从尼安德特人遗传而来的。”

paras.en: That's a satisfying conclusion to some clever anthropological detective work, but the variant's association with brain anatomy raised even more questions.
paras.zh: 对于一些聪明的人类学侦探工作来说，这是一个令人满意的结论，但该变异与大脑解剖学的关联引发了更多问题。

paras.en: Because although Neanderthals are thought to have had proportionally larger occipital lobes than modern humans, modern humans with the deletion have smaller occipital lobe volumes – about 0.85 cubic centimeters per copy of the variant.
paras.zh: 因为尽管人们认为尼安德特人的枕叶比例比现代人类大，但具有缺失的现代人类的枕叶体积较小——每个变体副本约 0.85 立方厘米。

paras.en: The researchers suggest that this apparent contradiction may not be a contradiction at all.
paras.zh: 研究人员认为，这种明显的矛盾可能根本不是矛盾。

paras.en: "Brain anatomy is influenced by many genes and other factors, including eye and body size," Zeberg explained. "A single Neanderthal variant need not reflect the overall anatomy of Neanderthals."
paras.zh: “大脑解剖结构受到许多基因和其他因素的影响，包括眼睛和身体大小，”泽伯格解释说。 “单一的尼安德特人变体不需要反映尼安德特人的整体解剖结构。”

paras.en: The researchers also found that the deletion wasn't just associated with anatomy. As with any aspect of an organ as complicated as the brain, it's natural to wonder whether a difference in its structure might be reflected in how it functions.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现，这种缺失不仅仅与解剖学有关。与大脑这样复杂的器官的任何方面一样，人们很自然地想知道其结构的差异是否会反映在其功能上。

paras.en: The researchers dug into existing genetic data from the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium, which studies the genetic contributions to psychiatric disorders, to look for associations with the Neanderthal variant.
paras.zh: 研究人员深入研究了精神病基因组学联盟的现有遗传数据，以寻找与尼安德特人变异的关联，该联盟研究精神疾病的遗传贡献。

paras.en: They found that people carrying the variant had slightly lower odds of schizophrenia – around 5 percent lower per copy, or nearly 10 percent for people with two copies.
paras.zh: 他们发现，携带该变体的人患精神分裂症的几率略低——每份拷贝的人患精神分裂症的几率要低约 5%，而携带两份拷贝的人患精神分裂症的几率则要低近 10%。

paras.en: But they did not establish whether this was linked to the volume of the occipital lobe.
paras.zh: 但他们没有确定这是否与枕叶的体积有关。

paras.en: "One possibility is that the variant influences brain development through the gene DAAM1," Zeberg said. "Whether the reduced schizophrenia risk is directly related to the smaller occipital lobe remains, at least for us, unknown."
paras.zh: Zeberg 说：“一种可能性是，该变异通过 DAAM1 基因影响大脑发育。” “精神分裂症风险降低是否与枕叶较小直接相关，至少对我们来说，仍然未知。”

paras.en: And, intriguingly, the researchers found no significant association with general intelligence, and little or no meaningful association with educational attainment.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，研究人员发现与一般智力没有显着关联，与教育程度几乎没有或没有有意义的关联。

paras.en: "These findings caution against equating the size of a brain region with cognitive abilities," they write.
paras.zh: 他们写道：“这些发现警告不要将大脑区域的大小与认知能力等同起来。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上。

articles.title: NASA is offering $1 million for bold ideas to help build a Moon base

paras.en: NASA is offering $1 million for bold ideas to help build a Moon base
paras.zh: NASA 将为帮助建立月球基地的大胆想法提供 100 万美元

paras.en: - NASA is offering $1 million in its new Moon Base Challenge, inviting U.S. students to develop innovative solutions for building humanityâs first permanent lunar outpost. From power systems to astronaut safety, their ideas could help make long-term life on the Moon possible and pave the way to Mars.
paras.zh: - NASA 将在其新的月球基地挑战赛中提供 100 万美元，邀请美国学生开发创新解决方案，以建造人类第一个永久月球前哨站。从电力系统到宇航员安全，他们的想法可以帮助人们在月球上长期生活并为前往火星铺平道路。

paras.en: NASA has launched a $1 million Moon Base Challenge, inviting teams of students from high schools and colleges across the United States to help develop ideas for humanity's future on the Moon. The competition was announced during a MAX POWER event at Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Florida. Presented as part of a Golden Age of Science, the initiative gives young innovators an opportunity to contribute designs and potential solutions for NASA's planned lunar base.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局发起了一项价值 100 万美元的月球基地挑战赛，邀请来自美国各地高中和大学的学生团队帮助为人类在月球上的未来制定想法。此次竞赛是在佛罗里达州肯尼迪航天中心游客中心举行的 MAX POWER 活动期间宣布的。作为科学黄金时代的一部分，该倡议为年轻的创新者提供了为美国宇航局计划的月球基地贡献设计和潜在解决方案的机会。

paras.en: "We're looking for students ready to think creatively, work as a team, and take on real problems connected to NASA's future on the Moon," said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. "You do not have to wait until graduation to contribute. Curiosity, creativity, and the willingness to tackle hard problems without obvious answers are exactly the qualities we need as we build what comes next."
paras.zh: NASA 局长贾里德·艾萨克曼 (Jared Isaacman) 表示：“我们正在寻找愿意创造性思考、团队合作并解决与 NASA 月球未来相关的实际问题的学生。” “你不必等到毕业才能做出贡献。好奇心、创造力以及在没有明显答案的情况下解决难题的意愿正是我们在构建未来产品时所需要的品质。”

paras.en: NASA is working toward establishing a Moon Base near the lunar South Pole, where astronauts will be able to live, conduct research, and explore the surrounding region. Creating a lasting human presence on the Moon is also an important step toward future missions that will carry astronauts to Mars. Achieving these goals will require expertise and creative thinking from people across a wide range of industries and disciplines.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局正在努力在月球南极附近建立一个月球基地，宇航员将能够在那里生活、进行研究和探索周边地区。在月球上建立人类持久存在也是迈向未来将宇航员送上火星的任务的重要一步。实现这些目标需要来自各个行业和学科的人们的专业知识和创造性思维。

paras.en: "As we build and design the foundations of Moon Base, we want to leverage all the ingenuity and innovation to think of every consideration our explorers might need to live and work there," said Carlos García-Galán, manager, Moon Base Program. "Students bring exactly the bold ideas that we're looking for, and I'm looking forward to their fresh perspective. Ultimately, Moon Base is for them, people who will experience a world where humans are on the Moon to stay."
paras.zh: 月球基地项目经理卡洛斯·加西亚-加兰 (Carlos García-Galán) 表示：“当我们建造和设计月球基地的基础时，我们希望利用所有的独创性和创新性来考虑我们的探险家在那里生活和工作可能需要的每一个因素。” “学生们带来的正是我们正在寻找的大胆想法，我期待着他们的新鲜视角。最终，月球基地是为他们准备的，他们将体验人类在月球上居住的世界。”

paras.en: Six Major Challenges of Living on the Moon
paras.zh: 生活在月球上的六大挑战

paras.en: The competition will unfold in multiple phases, with student teams developing solutions to six essential aspects of operating a lunar base. These include generating and storing power, constructing facilities, maintaining life support systems, enabling transportation across the lunar surface, establishing communications networks, and protecting astronauts.
paras.zh: 竞赛将分多个阶段进行，学生团队将针对运营月球基地的六个基本方面开发解决方案。其中包括发电和储存电力、建设设施、维护生命支持系统、实现月球表面的运输、建立通信网络和保护宇航员。

paras.en: Each category addresses practical obstacles that NASA must overcome to support long-term operations on the Moon. By working on these problems, students can explore new approaches to lunar technologies while developing technical and professional skills that could prepare them for careers in aerospace and related fields.
paras.zh: 每个类别都解决了美国宇航局必须克服的实际障碍，以支持月球上的长期运作。通过解决这些问题，学生可以探索月球技术的新方法，同时培养技术和专业技能，为他们在航空航天和相关领域的职业做好准备。

paras.en: The challenge is designed around actual environmental conditions and mission requirements that would affect daily life and operations on the lunar surface. Participants will produce work similar to that used in the space industry, including evaluations of competing technical options, proposals outlining potential designs, and presentations for project stakeholders.
paras.zh: 该挑战是围绕影响月球表面日常生活和操作的实际环境条件和任务要求而设计的。参与者将制作类似于航天工业中使用的作品，包括对竞争技术选项的评估、概述潜在设计的提案以及为项目利益相关者进行的演示。

paras.en: Students from technical, vocational, and other academic backgrounds are encouraged to participate. Previous specialized knowledge of engineering or related technical fields is not required, making the competition accessible to a broad range of young innovators.
paras.zh: 鼓励来自技术、职业和其他学术背景的学生参与。不需要具备工程或相关技术领域的专业知识，因此比赛适合广泛的年轻创新者。

paras.en: Inspiring the Next Generation of Space Explorers
paras.zh: 激励下一代太空探索者

paras.en: Beyond generating ideas for the Moon Base, NASA hopes the competition will help develop the skills needed by the next generation of aerospace professionals. By exposing students to practical design challenges, the agency aims to encourage collaboration, creative problem-solving, and greater involvement in future space exploration.
paras.zh: 除了为月球基地提供创意之外，美国宇航局希望此次竞赛能够帮助培养下一代航空航天专业人士所需的技能。通过让学生面临实际的设计挑战，该机构旨在鼓励协作、创造性地解决问题以及更多地参与未来的太空探索。

paras.en: "Students are the next generation of explorers and innovators. Their unique perspectives are key to helping us envision a future away from Earth, and I'm excited to see the creativity and ingenuity spurred by this challenge," said Elaine Ho, associate administrator for the Office of STEM Engagement at NASA Headquarters.
paras.zh: NASA 总部 STEM 参与办公室副主任 Elaine Ho 表示：“学生是下一代探索者和创新者。他们独特的视角是帮助我们畅想远离地球的未来的关键，我很高兴看到这一挑战激发出创造力和独创性。”

paras.en: How to Enter NASA's $1 Million Moon Base Challenge
paras.zh: 如何参加 NASA 的 100 万美元月球基地挑战赛

paras.en: Interested student teams must register through the NASA STEM Gateway. Registration remains open until January 25, 2027.
paras.zh: 有兴趣的学生团队必须通过 NASA STEM Gateway 注册。注册截止日期为 2027 年 1 月 25 日。

paras.en: NASA's Office of STEM Engagement developed the competition in partnership with the agency's Moon Base Program. The Institute of Competition Sciences is responsible for administering the challenge under a contract with NASA's Center of Excellence for Collaborative Innovation, which operates within the Research and Technology Mission Directorate.
paras.zh: NASA 的 STEM 参与办公室与该机构的月球基地计划合作举办了这项竞赛。竞争科学研究所负责根据与 NASA 协作创新卓越中心签订的合同管理此项挑战，该中心在研究和技术任务理事会内运作。

articles.title: Scientists discover that the heart doesn't age the way we thought

paras.en: Scientists discover that the heart doesn't age the way we thought
paras.zh: 科学家发现心脏并不像我们想象的那样衰老

paras.en: - Scientists have discovered that the heart ages unevenly, with surprising hotspots of inflammation and scarring concentrated in the valves and major blood vessels rather than the heart muscle. The findings challenge long-standing assumptions about cardiac aging and could help researchers develop new ways to protect the heart as we grow older.
paras.zh: - 科学家发现心脏老化不均匀，令人惊讶的炎症和疤痕热点集中在瓣膜和主要血管而不是心肌。这些发现挑战了长期以来关于心脏衰老的假设，并可以帮助研究人员开发新的方法来随着年龄的增长保护心脏。

paras.en: As the heart gets older, inflammation increases, but scientists have not fully understood where these changes occur or which parts of the organ are most affected. Researchers at The Jackson Laboratory (JAX) have now uncovered a surprising pattern: Certain regions of the heart appear to be hotspots for aging-related inflammation, offering new clues about how the heart changes over time.
paras.zh: 随着心脏老化，炎症会增加，但科学家尚未完全了解这些变化发生在哪里或器官的哪些部分受影响最大。杰克逊实验室 (JAX) 的研究人员现在发现了一种令人惊讶的模式：心脏的某些区域似乎是与衰老相关的炎症的热点区域，这为了解心脏如何随时间变化提供了新的线索。

paras.en: In a study of mouse hearts published in Aging Cell, the researchers discovered that signs of inflammation and tissue scarring were especially concentrated around the aortic valves and aortic root. These areas contain immune cells and connective tissue cells whose interactions change with age, potentially affecting the surrounding heart muscle. The findings provide a new picture of cardiac aging and could guide future efforts to understand cardiovascular disease.
paras.zh: 在《衰老细胞》上发表的一项针对小鼠心脏的研究中，研究人员发现炎症和组织疤痕的迹象尤其集中在主动脉瓣和主动脉根部周围。这些区域含有免疫细胞和结缔组织细胞，它们的相互作用随着年龄的增长而变化，可能会影响周围的心肌。这些发现提供了心脏衰老的新图景，并可以指导未来了解心血管疾病的努力。

paras.en: "Some of the markers associated with inflammaging were there from the very beginning in young hearts, but they were focused specifically in areas no one had defined before, in the valves and the aorta rather than in muscle tissue," said study author Nadia Rosenthal, scientific director at JAX. "We really have to think of aging as something that is not linear, because just like we know that people don't age at the same rate, what we know now is that organs and tissues don't age at the same rate either, even within one individual."
paras.zh: 研究作者、JAX 科学主任纳迪亚·罗森塔尔 (Nadia Rosenthal) 表示：“一些与炎症相关的标记从一开始就存在于年轻的心脏中，但它们专门集中在以前没有人定义过的区域，即瓣膜和主动脉，而不是肌肉组织。” “我们确实必须将衰老视为非线性的事情，因为就像我们知道人们不会以相同的速度衰老一样，我们现在知道器官和组织也不会以相同的速度衰老，即使在一个人体内也是如此。”

paras.en: Much of the previous research on heart aging has centered on cardiac muscle, particularly the left ventricle. This chamber performs the essential task of pumping blood into the aorta and throughout the body. By studying the heart as a whole, rather than concentrating primarily on its muscle, the JAX team uncovered important changes in other tissues and the ways their cells interact.
paras.zh: 之前关于心脏衰老的大部分研究都集中在心肌，特别是左心室。该腔室执行将血液泵入主动脉和全身的基本任务。通过研究整个心脏，而不是主要关注其肌肉，JAX 团队发现了其他组织及其细胞相互作用方式的重要变化。

paras.en: "The valves and the major blood vessels are parts often thought of as plumbing rather than the main engine, but this is a very complicated little machine," Rosenthal said. "It turns out they're home to many of the cells we're interested in, and that's where some of the most important aging-related signals were concentrated."
paras.zh: 罗森塔尔说：“阀门和主要血管通常被认为是管道部件，而不是主机，但这是一台非常复杂的小机器。” “事实证明，它们是我们感兴趣的许多细胞的家园，也是一些最重要的衰老相关信号集中的地方。”

paras.en: Growing older is the single greatest risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet many of the cellular processes responsible for the heart's decline remain poorly understood. One challenge is that mammalian heart muscle cells have very little ability to regenerate or replace themselves. To investigate what happens as the heart ages, Rosenthal and her colleagues used advanced techniques that allowed them to study thousands of individual cells from young and old mice while also identifying their locations within the heart.
paras.zh: 年龄增长是心血管疾病的最大单一危险因素，但许多导致心脏衰退的细胞过程仍然知之甚少。一项挑战是哺乳动物心肌细胞的再生或替换能力非常弱。为了研究心脏老化时会发生什么，罗森塔尔和她的同事使用了先进的技术，使他们能够研究来自年轻和年老小鼠的数千个单个细胞，同时确定它们在心脏内的位置。

paras.en: Scientists already know that aging is accompanied by a persistent, low level of inflammation throughout the body. Earlier studies have found similar changes in the heart, including an increase in immune cells that regulate inflammatory activity (macrophages) and cells that produce and maintain connective tissue and contribute to scar formation (fibroblasts).
paras.zh: 科学家们已经知道，衰老伴随着全身持续、低水平的炎症。早期的研究发现心脏也有类似的变化，包括调节炎症活动的免疫细胞（巨噬细胞）和产生和维持结缔组织并有助于疤痕形成的细胞（成纤维细胞）的增加。

paras.en: The new analysis showed that aging macrophages became more active in genes involved in inflammation and changes to tissue structure. Fibroblasts, meanwhile, increasingly displayed molecular characteristics associated with fibrosis (or scarring). Crucially, the researchers went beyond identifying which genes were active. They also mapped the locations of these cells, making it possible to see how different regions of the heart change as they grow older.
paras.zh: 新的分析表明，衰老的巨噬细胞在涉及炎症和组织结构变化的基因中变得更加活跃。与此同时，成纤维细胞越来越多地表现出与纤维化（或疤痕）相关的分子特征。至关重要的是，研究人员不仅仅确定哪些基因是活跃的。他们还绘制了这些细胞的位置图，从而可以了解心脏不同区域随着年龄的增长如何变化。

paras.en: This approach revealed that inflammation and fibrosis (or scarring) were not distributed uniformly. Instead, the strongest signals appeared around the heart valves and aortic root. The researchers believe these regions may act as important centers of cardiac aging, where changes in supporting cells could influence the health of nearby heart muscle.
paras.zh: 这种方法揭示了炎症和纤维化（或疤痕）分布不均匀。相反，最强的信号出现在心脏瓣膜和主动脉根部周围。研究人员认为，这些区域可能是心脏衰老的重要中心，其中支持细胞的变化可能会影响附近心肌的健康。

paras.en: "To keep muscle cells happy, the other cells in the heart have to continue supporting them throughout life," Rosenthal said. "What this study does, for the first time, is provide a comprehensive picture of how those support cells, particularly fibroblasts and macrophages, change with age and contribute to what we call inflammaging."
paras.zh: 罗森塔尔说：“为了让肌肉细胞保持快乐，心脏中的其他细胞必须在一生中继续支持它们。” “这项研究的目的是首次全面了解这些支持细胞，特别是成纤维细胞和巨噬细胞如何随着年龄的增长而变化，并导致我们所说的炎症。”

paras.en: Surprising Signs of Aging in Young Hearts
paras.zh: 年轻心灵中令人惊讶的衰老迹象

paras.en: Another unexpected discovery challenged assumptions about how scientists identify aging cells. The team examined molecular markers frequently associated with cellular senescence, a state in which cells permanently lose the ability to divide, often because of aging or stress. As senescent cells accumulate, they can contribute to ongoing inflammation, tissue damage, and diseases associated with older age.
paras.zh: 另一项意想不到的发现挑战了科学家如何识别衰老细胞的假设。研究小组检查了经常与细胞衰老相关的分子标记，细胞衰老是一种细胞永久失去分裂能力的状态，通常是由于衰老或压力。随着衰老细胞的积累，它们会导致持续的炎症、组织损伤和与老年相关的疾病。

paras.en: Surprisingly, some of these supposedly age-related markers were already present in young mouse hearts. Their presence suggests that the markers alone cannot reliably establish whether a cell has entered senescence, and that their meaning may depend on where they appear and the condition of the surrounding tissue.
paras.zh: 令人惊讶的是，其中一些被认为与年龄相关的标记物已经存在于年轻小鼠的心脏中。它们的存在表明，仅靠这些标记物无法可靠地确定细胞是否已进入衰老状态，并且它们的含义可能取决于它们出现的位置以及周围组织的状况。

paras.en: "What surprised us was that some of these markers that have been associated with aging were already present in young hearts. They weren't where anyone expected to find them, and that forced us to rethink what those markers are telling us," Rosenthal said. "That turns the usual interpretation of cardiac aging on its ear because these markers alone don't mean a cell is senescent. There's nothing senescent about a six-month-old mouse heart."
paras.zh: 罗森塔尔说：“令我们惊讶的是，其中一些与衰老相关的标记物已经存在于年轻的心脏中。它们并不在任何人期望的地方，这迫使我们重新思考这些标记物告诉我们什么。” “这改变了人们对心脏衰老的通常解释，因为这些标记本身并不意味着细胞衰老。六个月大的小鼠心脏没有任何衰老现象。”

paras.en: The researchers also identified genes that became more active with age and were especially prominent in the same regions. Among them were Ccl8, which helps transmit inflammatory signals, and Cdkn1a (also known as p21), a gene widely used as an indicator of cellular senescence. Their locations provided further evidence that the valves and aortic root may be particularly important areas for understanding how the heart ages.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现了随着年龄的增长而变得更加活跃的基因，并且在同一区域尤其突出。其中包括有助于传递炎症信号的 Ccl8 和广泛用作细胞衰老指标的基因 Cdkn1a（也称为 p21）。它们的位置进一步证明瓣膜和主动脉根可能是了解心脏如何老化的特别重要的区域。

paras.en: "We're not talking about single genes. We're talking about an entire conversation between immune cells and fibroblasts. As the heart ages, the way those cells communicate changes, and that shift appears to be linked to the inflammation and tissue remodeling we see in older hearts," Rosenthal said.
paras.zh: “我们不是在谈论单个基因。我们谈论的是免疫细胞和成纤维细胞之间的整个对话。随着心脏的老化，这些细胞沟通的方式会发生变化，而这种变化似乎与我们在老年心脏中看到的炎症和组织重塑有关，”罗森塔尔说。

paras.en: Male and Female Hearts Show Different Aging Patterns
paras.zh: 男性和女性心脏表现出不同的衰老模式

paras.en: The study uncovered another important distinction: Aging did not produce exactly the same molecular changes in male and female mouse hearts.
paras.zh: 该研究发现了另一个重要的区别：衰老并没有在雄性和雌性小鼠心脏中产生完全相同的分子变化。

paras.en: In males, aging fibroblasts showed stronger connections to biological processes associated with fibrosis. In females, the corresponding changes were more closely related to pathways involved in heart development and protein production.
paras.zh: 在男性中，衰老的成纤维细胞与纤维化相关的生物过程表现出更强的联系。在女性中，相应的变化与心脏发育和蛋白质产生的途径更为密切相关。

paras.en: Rosenthal noted that these differences may offer clues about cardiovascular aging in humans. Heart disease tends to become more common in women after menopause, while its development in men generally follows a more gradual pattern. The distinct cellular changes observed in male and female mice could help researchers investigate the biological processes behind these differences.
paras.zh: 罗森塔尔指出，这些差异可能为人类心血管衰老提供线索。心脏病在绝经后的女性中往往变得更加常见，而男性的心脏病的发展通常遵循更为渐进的模式。在雄性和雌性小鼠中观察到的不同细胞变化可以帮助研究人员研究这些差异背后的生物过程。

paras.en: However, the results describe differences in molecular activity, not demonstrated differences in heart function or disease risk. Further research will be needed to determine how these patterns influence cardiovascular health.
paras.zh: 然而，结果描述了分子活性的差异，并未证明心脏功能或疾病风险的差异。需要进一步的研究来确定这些模式如何影响心血管健康。

paras.en: To explore whether their findings might also apply to people, the team compared the mouse results with previously published data from human hearts. Several molecular processes associated with aging, including pathways involved in responding to cellular stress, appeared in both species. This overlap suggests that at least some of the biological changes identified in mice may also be relevant to human heart aging.
paras.zh: 为了探索他们的发现是否也适用于人类，研究小组将小鼠的结果与之前发布的人类心脏数据进行了比较。几个与衰老相关的分子过程，包括参与响应细胞应激的途径，都出现在这两个物种中。这种重叠表明，至少在小鼠身上发现的一些生物学变化也可能与人类心脏衰老有关。

paras.en: "Our findings change the focus from aging across the entire heart to specific anatomical hotspots, helping us better understand how inflammation and fibrosis are connected and which regions of the heart are involved in the aging process," said study author Amalia Sintou, a postdoctoral associate at JAX.
paras.zh: 研究作者、JAX 博士后研究员 Amalia Sintou 表示：“我们的研究结果将焦点从整个心脏的衰老转移到了特定的解剖热点，帮助我们更好地了解炎症和纤维化之间的关系，以及心脏的哪些区域参与了衰老过程。”

paras.en: Could These Discoveries Help Protect Aging Hearts?
paras.zh: 这些发现有助于保护衰老的心脏吗？

paras.en: Although the research does not yet identify a new treatment, it offers scientists a more detailed understanding of where aging-related changes occur and which cells are involved. By revealing these cellular patterns, the findings could help guide future studies aimed at reducing cardiovascular decline, maintaining healthy heart function, and improving health later in life.
paras.zh: 尽管该研究尚未确定新的治疗方法，但它使科学家能够更详细地了解与衰老相关的变化发生在何处以及涉及哪些细胞。通过揭示这些细胞模式，这些发现可以帮助指导未来旨在减少心血管衰退、维持健康的心脏功能和改善晚年健康的研究。

paras.en: Rosenthal's team is now examining whether exercise, diet, and disease alter the interactions between immune cells and connective tissue cells. The researchers hope to distinguish the normal effects of aging from changes that may leave the heart increasingly vulnerable to cardiovascular problems.
paras.zh: 罗森塔尔的团队目前正在研究运动、饮食和疾病是否会改变免疫细胞和结缔组织细胞之间的相互作用。研究人员希望区分衰老的正常影响和可能使心脏越来越容易受到心血管问题影响的变化。

paras.en: The experimental design also helped the team isolate aging itself as a contributing factor. Because the mice lived under the same conditions and received the same diet, the researchers could investigate age-related changes without the additional variation introduced by different environments or eating habits.
paras.zh: 实验设计还帮助团队将衰老本身作为一个促成因素。由于小鼠生活在相同的条件下并接受相同的饮食，因此研究人员可以研究与年龄相关的变化，而无需不同环境或饮食习惯带来的额外变化。

paras.en: "Valve replacement is common in older adults, and one of the big questions is how much of the underlying damage is driven by aging itself," said study author Aleksandra Aljakna Khan, a postdoctoral associate at JAX. "Because all of the mice in our study lived in the same environment and ate the same diet, we were able to isolate the effects of aging and show that aging alone can initiate some of these changes in the valves and aorta."
paras.zh: 研究作者、JAX 博士后助理 Aleksandra Aljakna Khan 表示：“瓣膜置换术在老年人中很常见，其中一个大问题是，有多少潜在损伤是由衰老本身造成的。” “因为我们研究中的所有小鼠都生活在相同的环境中并吃相同的饮食，所以我们能够分离出衰老的影响，并表明衰老本身就可以引发瓣膜和主动脉的一些变化。”

paras.en: Together, the findings suggest that understanding heart aging requires looking beyond the muscle responsible for pumping blood. The valves, major blood vessels, and supporting cells may play a much larger role than previously recognized. Learning how these structures change and communicate over time could eventually help scientists identify ways to preserve cardiovascular health as people age.
paras.zh: 总之，这些发现表明，了解心脏衰老需要超越负责泵血的肌肉。瓣膜、主要血管和支持细胞所发挥的作用可能比之前认识到的要大得多。了解这些结构如何随着时间的推移而变化和交流，最终可以帮助科学家找到随着人们年龄增长而保持心血管健康的方法。

paras.en: The research received funding from the NIH Common Fund through The Jackson Laboratory Senescence Tissue Mapping Center (JAX-Sen TMC U54 AG079753). Additional support came from JAX's National Cancer Institute-designated Cancer Center (P30 CA034196).
paras.zh: 该研究通过杰克逊实验室衰老组织绘图中心 (JAX-Sen TMC U54 AG079753) 获得了 NIH 共同基金的资助。其他支持来自 JAX 国家癌症研究所指定的癌症中心 (P30 CA034196)。

paras.en: Additional authors from The Jackson Laboratory included Yue Zhao, Antonios Somarakis, Harshpreet Chandok, Juliana Alcoforado Diniz, Ramalakshmi Ramasamy, Gretchen T. Clark, Brian S. White, Paul Robson, Ron Korstanje, and J. Matthew Mahoney. Leon Frommer and Sikander Hayat of RWTH Aachen University also contributed to the study.
paras.zh: 杰克逊实验室的其他作者包括赵越、Antonios Somarakis、Harshpreet Chandok、Juliana Alcoforado Diniz、Ramalakshmi Ramasamy、Gretchen T. Clark、Brian S. White、Paul Robson、Ron Korstanje 和 J. Matthew Mahoney。亚琛工业大学的 Leon Frommer 和 Sikander Hayat 也对这项研究做出了贡献。

articles.title: Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder

paras.en: Vitamin B12 may hold the key to treating a rare genetic disorder
paras.zh: 维生素 B12 可能是治疗罕见遗传性疾病的关键

paras.en: - Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing
paras.zh: - 马克斯·普朗克衰老生物学研究所

paras.en: - Scientists discovered that vitamin B12 largely reversed developmental abnormalities in worms carrying a genetic mutation linked to Verheij syndrome, a rare disorder that causes growth problems and developmental delays. Similar metabolic changes were identified in human patients, raising the possibility that this common vitamin could inspire new treatments for rare genetic diseases.
paras.zh: - 科学家发现，维生素 B12 在很大程度上逆转了携带 Verheij 综合征相关基因突变的线虫的发育异常，Verheij 综合征是一种导致生长问题和发育迟缓的罕见疾病。在人类患者中也发现了类似的代谢变化，这增加了这种常见维生素可能激发罕见遗传疾病新疗法的可能性。

paras.en: A surprising discovery involving vitamin B12 could open new possibilities for understanding and potentially treating rare genetic disorders. Researchers found that the vitamin can correct developmental problems in tiny worms carrying a genetic mutation associated with Verheij syndrome, a rare human condition that causes developmental delays, impaired growth, and short stature.
paras.zh: 一项涉及维生素 B12 的惊人发现可能为理解和治疗罕见遗传性疾病开辟新的可能性。研究人员发现，这种维生素可以纠正携带 Verheij 综合征相关基因突变的小蠕虫的发育问题，Verheij 综合征是一种罕见的人类疾病，会导致发育迟缓、生长受损和身材矮小。

paras.en: The findings center on a cellular process called RNA splicing, which helps prepare the genetic instructions cells use to produce proteins. During splicing, unnecessary portions of messenger RNA are removed, and the remaining sections are joined together in the correct order. When this process goes wrong, it can disrupt essential cellular functions and contribute to serious developmental disorders.
paras.zh: 这些发现集中在一种称为RNA剪接的细胞过程上，该过程有助于准备细胞用来产生蛋白质的遗传指令。在剪接过程中，信使 RNA 中不必要的部分被去除，剩余部分以正确的顺序连接在一起。当这个过程出现问题时，它会破坏基本的细胞功能并导致严重的发育障碍。

paras.en: Mutations in genes responsible for splicing can cause conditions such as Verheij syndrome. To better understand the effects of these genetic changes, scientists investigated how a related mutation affects growth and metabolism in a laboratory model.
paras.zh: 负责剪接的基因突变可能导致 Verheij 综合征等疾病。为了更好地了解这些基因变化的影响，科学家们在实验室模型中研究了相关突变如何影响生长和新陈代谢。

paras.en: Vitamin B12 Reverses Developmental Defects in Worms
paras.zh: 维生素 B12 可逆转线虫的发育缺陷

paras.en: The discovery emerged from experiments involving C. elegans, a tiny roundworm commonly used in biological research. The researchers were initially searching for previously unknown genes that influence lifespan when they began examining a mutation in a gene involved in RNA splicing. The same gene is associated with Verheij syndrome in humans.
paras.zh: 这一发现来自对秀丽隐杆线虫的实验，秀丽隐杆线虫是一种常用于生物研究的微小蛔虫。当研究人员开始检查参与 RNA 剪接的基因突变时，他们最初是在寻找以前未知的影响寿命的基因。相同的基因与人类 Verheij 综合征相关。

paras.en: Worms carrying the mutation developed problems resembling important features of the human disorder. Their growth slowed considerably, and they remained smaller than normal.
paras.zh: 携带突变的蠕虫会出现与人类疾病的重要特征类似的问题。它们的生长速度显着放缓，并且仍然小于正常水平。

paras.en: To investigate why this happened, the scientists conducted genetic screens and analyzed the worms' metabolism. They discovered that the mutation disrupted specific metabolic pathways that depend on vitamin B12 and are essential for healthy growth and normal cellular activity.
paras.zh: 为了调查发生这种情况的原因，科学家们进行了基因筛查并分析了线虫的新陈代谢。他们发现，这种突变破坏了依赖维生素 B12 的特定代谢途径，这些途径对于健康生长和正常细胞活动至关重要。

paras.en: The researchers then tested whether providing additional vitamin B12 could counteract these changes. Remarkably, the treatment restored the affected metabolic processes to normal and corrected the developmental abnormalities associated with the mutation.
paras.zh: 研究人员随后测试了提供额外的维生素 B12 是否可以抵消这些变化。值得注意的是，这种治疗使受影响的代谢过程恢复正常，并纠正了与突变相关的发育异常。

paras.en: "We were surprised to find that a change in a fundamental process of RNA processing had such a targeted effect on vitamin B12-dependent metabolism," says Jonathan Kölschbach, first author of the study. "Even more exciting was that we were able to largely correct the consequences of this change in the worm model using vitamin B12."
paras.zh: 该研究的第一作者 Jonathan Kölschbach 表示：“我们惊讶地发现 RNA 加工基本过程的变化对维生素 B12 依赖性代谢产生了如此有针对性的影响。” “更令人兴奋的是，我们能够使用维生素 B12 很大程度上纠正线虫模型中这种变化的后果。”

paras.en: Could Vitamin B12 Help Treat a Rare Genetic Disorder?
paras.zh: 维生素 B12 能否帮助治疗罕见的遗传性疾病？

paras.en: To explore whether their findings might also apply to people, the researchers examined publicly available datasets from human cells. They also worked with Hormos Dafsari, a neuropediatrician at the University Hospital Cologne, to collect blood samples from patients diagnosed with Verheij syndrome.
paras.zh: 为了探索他们的发现是否也适用于人类，研究人员检查了来自人类细胞的公开数据集。他们还与科隆大学医院的神经儿科医生霍尔莫斯·达夫萨里 (Hormos Dafsari) 合作，从诊断为 Verheij 综合征的患者身上采集血液样本。

paras.en: These investigations uncovered evidence of similar metabolic changes in humans, suggesting that the vitamin B12-related pathways affected in the worms may also play a role in the human disorder.
paras.zh: 这些研究发现了人类类似代谢变化的证据，表明线虫中受影响的维生素 B12 相关途径也可能在人类疾病中发挥作用。

paras.en: Although the results are promising, researchers have not yet established whether vitamin B12 supplementation can improve symptoms in people with Verheij syndrome. Additional studies will be necessary to determine whether the benefits observed in worms can be translated into a treatment for patients.
paras.zh: 尽管结果令人鼓舞，但研究人员尚未确定补充维生素 B12 是否可以改善 Verheij 综合征患者的症状。还需要进行更多的研究来确定在线虫中观察到的益处是否可以转化为对患者的治疗。

paras.en: The discovery also raises a broader possibility. Metabolic disruptions may contribute more substantially to diseases caused by faulty RNA splicing than scientists previously recognized. Understanding these connections could help researchers identify new therapeutic strategies, potentially extending beyond Verheij syndrome to other rare genetic conditions.
paras.zh: 这一发现还提出了更广泛的可能性。代谢紊乱对 RNA 剪接错误引起的疾病的影响可能比科学家之前认识到的更大。了解这些联系可以帮助研究人员确定新的治疗策略，有可能从 Verheij 综合征扩展到其他罕见的遗传疾病。

paras.en: "Our study is a good example of how basic research on model organisms can provide new insights into human diseases," says Adam Antebi, Director at the Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing and lead author of the study. "A fundamental biological question can thus give rise to a new approach that could also become medically relevant in the long term."
paras.zh: 马克斯·普朗克衰老生物学研究所所长、该研究的主要作者 Adam Antebi 表示：“我们的研究是一个很好的例子，说明模式生物的基础研究如何为人类疾病提供新的见解。” “因此，一个基本的生物学问题可以产生一种新的方法，从长远来看，这种方法也可能在医学上具有相关性。”

paras.en: Materials provided by Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由马克斯·普朗克衰老生物学研究所提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。
